title: Extension of a local finite free map from an ideal lattice
statement: Let Z be integral Noetherian and G coherent [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-coherent]. Fix r ≥ 0, an open U containing the generic point ξ, and a map φ from the restriction of the finite free structure-module sheaf on ULift (Fin r) to G restricted to U. Suppose the stalk of φ at ξ in U is invertible [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. There exist a coherent ideal sheaf I on Z and χ from the coproduct of r copies of I.toModules to G whose stalk at ξ in Z is invertible [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

proof.text: Construct J as the vanishing ideal of Z minus U. The reduced induced closed subscheme theorem and the affine ideal-zero-set criterion identify the open where the ideal stalk is the unit ideal with U.

The finite free source E is coherent and G is quasi-coherent by the locally Noetherian criterion. Use the final extension clause of coherent_homs_over_open to extend φ from J^n E, with the restriction identity in that theorem.

Construct I as the actual ideal sheaf J ^ n. The affine power-range formula gives equal affine ranges for the recursive module power and I.toModules, including n = 0. Sheaf separatedness and the cokernel-kernel factorization give an isomorphism compatible with the inclusions. Tensoring with the power module preserves coproducts by the source tensor-Hom adjunction. The right unitors therefore identify its tensor product with the finite free module with a coproduct of copies of the power module. Whisker exchange and unitor naturality identify multiplication with the coproduct of the power inclusion. This map is mono because finite coproducts are biproducts, so its image is isomorphic to its source. Reindex ULift (Fin r) by Fin r to obtain the required ideal-sum isomorphism. The ideal module is quasi-coherent as the kernel of the structure module map to the closed-subscheme pushforward; that pushforward is quasi-coherent by the proved source closed-immersion theorem. The structure module is finite type by its single free generator and coherent by the locally Noetherian criterion, so the quasi-coherent submodule clause makes I coherent.

Transport the extension from coherent_homs_over_open along the explicit ideal-sum isomorphism to obtain χ. First use overFunctorEquiv and fullness of overEquiv to pass the given morphism on U.toScheme to the slice site, and transport the extension identity back by naturality and cancellation of the equivalence isomorphisms. The ideal-power inclusion restricts to an isomorphism by coherent_homs_over_open. Taking the stalk of the identity on U shows the extension stalk is the composition of that isomorphism with the given invertible stalk. The source restrictStalkNatIso conjugates the underlying abelian-group stalk maps. Bijectivity, and hence invertibility of the module stalk map, passes through this conjugacy. Finally the stalk of the ideal-sum isomorphism is invertible and composition gives the claimed invertible χ stalk. All coproduct and power calculations include r = 0 and n = 0.

theorem exists_generic_ideal_extension (Z : Scheme.{w}) [IsNoetherian Z]
    [IsIntegral Z] (G : Z.Modules)
    (hG : RingedSpace.IsCoherent Z.toRingedSpace G)
    (r : ℕ) (U : Z.Opens) (hx : genericPoint Z ∈ U)
    (φ : (restrictFunctor U.ι).obj
        (SheafOfModules.free (R := Z.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{w} (Fin r))) ⟶
      (restrictFunctor U.ι).obj G)
    (hφ : IsIso ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor U.toScheme.toRingedSpace
      (⟨genericPoint Z, hx⟩ : U.toScheme)).map φ)) :
    ∃ (I : Z.IdealSheafData),
      RingedSpace.IsCoherent Z.toRingedSpace I.toModules ∧
      ∃ (χ : (∐ fun _ : Fin r => I.toModules) ⟶ G),
        IsIso ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor Z.toRingedSpace
          (genericPoint Z)).map χ)
